subject: maths
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Keeping track without numbers
outcomes: Learner can keep track of a large collection using marks or tallies and check if anything is missing
misconceptions: Thinks counting is only possible if you know number names
hooks: Deba and Deep’s cows: mark the wall for each cow leaving the gate

topics.title: Counting in groups of 5 with tallies
outcomes: Learner can use tallies in groups of 5 to count quickly and compare totals
misconceptions: Counts each tally bundle as 1 instead of 5
hooks: Count names that start with each letter in your class

topics.title: Shapes in toys
outcomes: Learner can identify cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres used to build toys
misconceptions: Believes a shape with a curved face cannot have a flat face too
hooks: Channapatna toys and building blocks

topics.title: Faces and views
outcomes: Learner can predict what a toy looks like from the top, front and side
misconceptions: Thinks an object looks the same from every side
hooks: Look at a steel glass from above vs from the side

topics.title: Numbers up to 200
outcomes: Learner can read, write and represent numbers up to 200 using hundreds, tens and ones
misconceptions: Writes one hundred twenty-five as 10025
hooks: Bundles of 100 sticks; the 200-page notebook

topics.title: Making 100 and jumps on the number line
outcomes: Learner can make 100 in different ways and use jumps of 10 on a number line
misconceptions: Thinks 60 + 4 makes 100 because 6 + 4 = 10
hooks: Bholu jumps from 65 to 100

topics.title: Estimating near 100
outcomes: Learner can estimate quantities close to 100 and check by counting in tens
misconceptions: Believes estimating is just guessing without reasons
hooks: How many handfuls of chana make about 100?

topics.title: Addition and subtraction stories
outcomes: Learner can solve addition and subtraction word problems up to 99 and choose the operation from the situation
misconceptions: Looks for key words like "more" and always adds
hooks: Nani Maa’s balushahi and stamp collection

topics.title: Number tricks and games
outcomes: Learner can explain why a number trick or simple game strategy works
misconceptions: Thinks number tricks are magic and cannot be explained
hooks: The "make it 9" trick and NIM game with Nani Maa

topics.title: Jumps on the number line
outcomes: Learner can add and subtract by making jumps of 10 and 1 on a number line
misconceptions: Counts the starting number as the first jump
hooks: Frog jumping 10 at a time across lily pads

topics.title: Corners and sides of 2D shapes
outcomes: Learner can describe squares, rectangles and triangles by their sides and corners
misconceptions: Thinks a square is not a rectangle
Believes a shape is a triangle only if it "looks like a roof"
hooks: Find squares and rectangles in a chessboard and a window grill

topics.title: Making shapes from shapes
outcomes: Learner can combine and split shapes (tangram pieces) to make new shapes
misconceptions: Thinks the area changes when pieces are rearranged
hooks: Make a boat with tangram pieces

topics.title: Straight and curved edges
outcomes: Learner can sort shapes by straight and curved edges and draw shapes on dot grids
misconceptions: Believes a circle has one corner
hooks: Draw a rangoli on a dot grid

topics.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
outcomes: Learner can represent 3-digit numbers with hundreds, tens and ones and read them aloud
misconceptions: Writes three hundred five as 3005 or 35 (ignores zero as placeholder)
hooks: ₹100, ₹10 and ₹1 notes and coins

topics.title: Comparing 3-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can compare and order 3-digit numbers by looking at hundreds first
misconceptions: Thinks 299 > 301 because 9s are big
hooks: Which train is longer: 299 or 301 seats?

topics.title: Multiplication as equal groups and arrays
outcomes: Learner can represent equal groups and arrays as multiplication facts
misconceptions: Thinks multiplication is only repeated addition and cannot be pictured as an array
hooks: Rakhis in rows on a thali; sweets in boxes

topics.title: Building times tables
outcomes: Learner can build tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 using skip counting and patterns
misconceptions: Believes tables must be memorised and cannot be worked out
hooks: How many rakhis for 6 brothers, 3 each?

topics.title: Halves and quarters as equal shares
outcomes: Learner can show half and quarter of a shape or collection by making equal parts
misconceptions: Thinks any two parts are halves even if they are unequal
Believes a quarter is bigger than a half because 4 is bigger than 2
hooks: Share a roti fairly between two, then among four

topics.title: Half of a quantity
outcomes: Learner can find half and quarter of small collections and lengths
misconceptions: Thinks half of an odd number of objects is impossible
hooks: Half a dozen bananas

topics.title: Numbers up to 1000 on the number line
outcomes: Learner can locate and estimate 3-digit numbers on a number line between hundreds
misconceptions: Thinks the spaces between hundreds on a number line can be unequal
hooks: How many people fit in a school assembly?

topics.title: Patterns and puzzles with 3-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can continue number sequences going up or down by 1, 10 or 100
misconceptions: Changes the wrong digit when adding 10 (e.g. 457 + 10 = 458)
hooks: Birbal and the crows of the city

topics.title: Measuring length in metres and centimetres
outcomes: Learner can estimate and measure lengths using a metre scale and centimetres
misconceptions: Starts measuring from 1 on the scale instead of 0
hooks: Measure the length of a dupatta or the classroom door

topics.title: Half and quarter metre
outcomes: Learner can use half and quarter metre to describe lengths
misconceptions: Thinks half a metre is 50 m
hooks: Ribbon pieces for decorating the class party

topics.title: Capacity in litres
outcomes: Learner can compare capacities and measure in litres and half litres
misconceptions: Believes a taller container always holds more
hooks: How many glasses fill a 1-litre milk packet?

topics.title: Weight in kilograms
outcomes: Learner can compare weights using a balance and kilogram weights
misconceptions: Thinks a kilogram of cotton is lighter than a kilogram of iron
hooks: Weighing atta and onions at the kirana shop

topics.title: Adding 3-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can add 3-digit numbers with regrouping using hundreds, tens and ones
misconceptions: Forgets to carry and writes each column sum, e.g. 158 + 67 = 1115
hooks: Kishan’s plant nursery saplings

topics.title: Subtracting 3-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can subtract 3-digit numbers by "opening" a hundred or a ten when needed
misconceptions: Subtracts smaller digit from bigger digit in every column
Does not know what to do when there is a zero to borrow from (e.g. 403 - 127)
hooks: Saplings left after packing an order

topics.title: Exchange, barter and money
outcomes: Learner can explain why money replaced barter and solve simple buying problems
misconceptions: Thinks things that are bigger always cost more
hooks: A hawa mithai vs a toffee at the haat

topics.title: Reading the clock
outcomes: Learner can read time to the hour, half hour and quarter hour on an analog clock
misconceptions: Mixes up the hour and minute hands
Reads the minute hand pointing at 3 as "3 minutes"
hooks: What time does your school bell ring?

topics.title: Calendar and durations
outcomes: Learner can find the number of days between two dates on a calendar
misconceptions: Counts both start and end days incorrectly when finding duration
hooks: How many days till Diwali vacation?

topics.title: Symmetry in designs
outcomes: Learner can identify objects and designs that look the same on both sides of a line
misconceptions: Thinks a design is symmetrical only if it is a vertical line
hooks: Malas, pottery and phulkari at the Surajkund mela

topics.title: Patterns in beads and tiles
outcomes: Learner can find the number of ways to make patterns with given beads and explain how they know all are found
misconceptions: Believes the same arrangement read backwards is a different pattern
hooks: Make malas with 4 red and 4 blue beads
